rationale: PINS the `imports` CONTRACT, which had no fixture coverage and no oracle at all before round 7. The analyzer emitted `imports` for every import_spec since GO18 and go's own requiredKinds has named the label since the wave, yet nothing compared it: the label was absent from the compared set, so 2,214 distinct import targets across 6,836 files were entirely outside the differential. Each case below is a shape a derivation can plausibly get wrong, and the FORBID half is what makes them constraints rather than a snapshot: an oracle that published the ALIAS instead of the path, or that skipped any spec carrying a `name` field, would satisfy every expect row while the real module path went unchecked. `C` is cgo's pseudo-package and `_ "embed"` is the embed generator — one-character and name-bearing specs are exactly the two the resolvable-path derivations drop, and together they are 313 rows in the pinned corpora. The paths are asserted VERBATIM including `golang.org/x/net/context` and `github.com/go-logr/logr`, because the separators (/ . -) are the whole reason the label moved off `references` in the first place: an oracle that normalised or truncated a path would agree on `fmt` and disagree on every real module path in the corpus. Every line below was read back from live emission with script/m14/tmp/god9-dump.ts, never predicted.
